author: Faulde, Franz
title: Historische Untersuchungen zur Marneschlacht 1914 (Die Sendung des Oberstleutnants Hentsch)
notes: A doctoral dissertation of 1925 given entirely to the Hentsch mission of 8–10 September 1914 — the one work in this registry whose whole subject is the contested point in 1914:historiography-hentsch-authority. Filed as a study by its form: an independent source-critical monograph, not an official history, though it works almost wholly on the official material. Its value here is that it reads the surviving evidence *as* evidence: it sets Tappen's four reports beside Dommes's recollections and shows the two accounts of Moltke's verbal order borrowing each other's wording between 1917 and 1920, which is why the wording of that order is quoted on the card as a recollection and not as a text. It is also this pack's only readable route to Müller-Loebnitz's Die Sendung des Oberstleutnants Hentsch and to Kuhl's Der Marnefeldzug, both of which Faulde quotes by page; the pack cites Faulde for what Faulde says, and names those works as unread. Partisan in one direction that the reader should know: Faulde argues for Bülow's influence as the centre of the affair and is correspondingly sceptical of Hentsch's own two reports. Pagination: the scan prints only two legible folios, '— 48 —' on leaf 50 and a damaged '— 3[1] —' on leaf 33, both giving a leaf-to-page offset of 2; the Inhaltsangabe's section ranges (Der Auftrag 17–29, Hentsch in Mareuil 39–50, Hentsch auf dem Rückwege 50–52) fall on that offset at four boundaries. Every page cited from it was read on the leaf that offset gives and its quoted phrase grepped back.
